run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The cart service is failing: the cart pod cart-74587775fc-lqsjt (node sregym-worker) is in CrashLoopBackOff (restartCount 5 at ~10:25:54; container last terminated with exitCode 139 reason Error; at 10:22:16 it was not ready with restarts already accumulating). Its own container stderr inside the sampled window (10:22:00 and 10:22:01) shows 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' thrown from cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected -> Initialize (Program.Main), i.e. the .NET process aborts at startup because it cannot open a connection to its valkey-cart (Redis) dependency. Because cart never stays listening, callers fail: frontend spans at 10:22:06-10:22:10 show POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout returning HTTP 500 with grpc '14 UNAVAILABLE ... connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.11.50:8080' (the cart Service ClusterIP), checkout's own oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder erroring on 'cart failure ... connection refused', and frontend-proxy POST plus load-generator POST returning 500. The dependency was checked and looks healthy: valkey-cart pod is Running/ready with 0 restarts and its logs show 'Ready to accept connections tcp' at 10:21:11; the valkey-cart Service (10.96.92.42:6379) has the correct endpoint (10.244.7.242:6379 = the valkey pod); no NetworkPolicies exist and all nodes are Ready without pressure. Cart itself was healthy until it was replaced: cart spans at 10:21:37-10:21:51 (including valkey-cart:6379 client spans of 0.36-1.68 ms and a successful checkout PlaceOrder) ran on the previous pod cart-74587775fc-rbrwk, which was stopped at 10:21:52 on sregym-worker3; the replacement pod's init container still reached valkey-cart 10.96.92.42:6379 at 10:21:53, yet every subsequent cart container instance fails to open a Redis connection. So the immediate failure mechanism is established (cart cannot connect to valkey-cart at startup -> crash loop -> cart Service refuses connections -> frontend cart/checkout 500s), but the fault that broke the cart->valkey-cart connection path between 10:21:53 and 10:22:00 is not directly observable with the available sources: no chaos/fault-injection object is visible, the change-history integration is not available, and the Redis integration could not authenticate to valkey (REDIS_AUTH_FAILED) so valkey's internal state could not be read. Flag-based fault injection is not enabled in the flagd-config configmap that was read (every flag on its off value). No error-rate or latency baseline exists for this environment (span-metric series first appear at 10:22:13), so no trend is claimed.

claims.text: The cart pod cart-74587775fc-lqsjt on node sregym-worker is crash-looping: at ~10:25:54 its container state was waiting with reason CrashLoopBackOff and restartCount 5; earlier at 10:22:18 its container status showed restartCount 2, ready=false, lastState terminated with exitCode 139 reason Error, and a following instance also terminated with exitCode 139 (finishedAt 10:22:17).

The cart container's own stderr at 10:22:00 and 10:22:01 (inside the sampled window) reads 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' with the stack cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected (ValkeyCartStore.cs:line 101) -> cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.Initialize (line 71) -> Program.Main (Program.cs:line 98), i.e. the cart process aborts because it cannot open a Redis connection at startup.

In the same pod, the init container wait-for-valkey-cart logged 'valkey-cart (10.96.92.42:6379) open' at 10:21:53.678, so reaching the valkey-cart Service address from that pod's network namespace succeeded seconds before the cart container's Redis connection failures.

Frontend error spans at 10:22:06-10:22:10 show POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout with http.status_code 500 and otel.status_code ERROR, whose error details are '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.11.50:8080' and '13 INTERNAL: cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout: rpc error: code = Unavailable ... dial tcp 10.96.11.50:8080: connect: connection refused'; the same sampled traces contain frontend oteldemo.CartService/AddItem (rpc.grpc.status_code 14), checkout oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (14) and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (13) errors, frontend-proxy POST 500 and load-generator POST 500.

The cart Service is ClusterIP 10.96.11.50 port 8080/targetPort 8080 with Endpoints subset 10.244.234.146:8080 (cart pod cart-74587775fc-lqsjt); the valkey-cart Service is ClusterIP 10.96.92.42 port 6379/targetPort 6379 with Endpoints subset 10.244.7.242:6379, which is the IP of pod valkey-cart-859985f49d-d8xzh.

valkey-cart-859985f49d-d8xzh is Running with 0 restarts and its logs in the window show 'Valkey version=9.0.1 ... just started', 'Warning: no config file specified, using the default config', 'Server initialized' and 'Ready to accept connections tcp' at 10:21:11, with no error or restart lines after that in the sampled window.

There are no NetworkPolicy objects in the cluster, and all four nodes (sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3) report Ready=True with no MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable=False.

Cart was working before the pod was replaced: cart spans between 10:21:37 and 10:21:51 show POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, AddItem and EmptyCart with no error status together with valkey-cart:6379 client spans of 0.363-1.680 ms, and a checkout trace in that period completed PlaceOrder with rpc.grpc.status_code 0.

Events show the previous cart pod cart-74587775fc-rbrwk being stopped on node sregym-worker3 ('Killing / Stopping container cart', 10:21:52) while the current cart pod cart-74587775fc-lqsjt (owner ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc) was created at 10:21:52 on node sregym-worker; the other astronomy-shop Unhealthy events in the window concern grafana, opensearch-0 and otel-collector-agent pods, not cart application containers.

The cart Deployment's container spec carries VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, a memory limit of 160Mi and no readiness/liveness/startup probes, and its pod template was unchanged when the pod was replaced (same ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc).

The flagd-config configmap read at 10:22:27 has every demo fault flag on its off value (cartFailure off, failedReadinessProbe off, productCatalogFailure off, recommendationCacheFailure off, adFailure off, paymentFailure off, paymentUnreachable off, kafkaQueueProblems off, emailMemoryLeak off, imageSlowLoad off, adHighCpu off, adManualGc off, llmInaccurateResponse off, llmRateLimitError off), and that configmap was last applied by manager helm at 2026-11-24T10:21:09Z.

All 23 astronomy-shop Deployments (including cart and valkey-cart) were created at 2026-11-24T10:21:09Z, and traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="cart"} has a single sample at 10:22:13 (value 39) with no earlier samples in the sampled window, so no pre-incident error-rate or latency baseline exists for this run.

A valkey-cart-side crash, OOM or restart is not supported: the valkey-cart pod is Running and ready with 0 restarts, its lastState is empty, its logs show it started and is accepting TCP connections with the default configuration, and both its Service and Endpoints point at the running pod's 10.244.7.242:6379.
A feature-flag-injected cart fault is not supported: the flagd-config configmap in effect lists cartFailure and failedReadinessProbe with defaultVariant off, and no other demo flag is on.

A node-level or policy-level network block is not supported by the objects checked: no NetworkPolicies exist and all nodes are Ready without pressure, and other cross-node calls in the same traces (product-catalog on sregym-worker to the postgresql Service on sregym-worker3) complete with rpc.grpc.status_code 0.

Rejected: the cart crash loop is caused by a cart container OOM kill or by its 160Mi memory limit. The container's termination reason is Error with exitCode 139 (not OOMKilled) and no OOM or Evicted pod events were observed.

The cart->valkey-cart connection path broke at approximately 10:21:52-10:22:00 rather than valkey-cart being down: the old cart pod kept serving with established valkey client calls of 0.363-1.680 ms until it was stopped at 10:21:52, the replacement pod's init container still connected to the valkey-cart Service at 10:21:53, but every new cart container instance afterwards fails to establish a Redis connection and aborts; a network-level fault (delay, loss or partition) between the cart pod and valkey-cart, or a dependency-side refusal of new Redis sessions, would fit this evidence, but the injecting object itself was not observed.

The replacement of the previous cart pod cart-74587775fc-rbrwk at 10:21:52 (Killing event from the kubelet on sregym-worker3, same ReplicaSet so no template change) is a separate pod-level event whose trigger is not visible in the available evidence; it is the moment the new pod that cannot connect to Redis was created, but no object applying that change was observed.

Check the fault-injection/chaos controller and any network shaping applied to the cart pod or to valkey-cart around 10:21:52-10:22:00 (for example delay, loss or partition experiments), since valkey-cart itself, its Service, its Endpoints and all nodes show no fault.

Capture the full StackExchange.Redis failure detail from the cart container (connection timeout versus authentication versus DNS) by reading the cart container logs of the later crash instances, which fall after 2026-11-24T10:22:13 and were therefore outside this run's authorized window.

gaps: The object that applied the fault to the cart->valkey-cart connection path was not observed: no chaos/fault-injection CRs or pods are visible among the pods read (only cart, valkey-cart and the standard app/observability pods exist), and the change_history integration is not available in this run.

Cart container logs after 2026-11-24T10:22:13 (the later crash instances, including the terminations at 10:22:17 and 10:22:52) fall outside the authorized window, so the underlying Redis client exception text could not be read; only the generic 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' line from 10:22:00-10:22:01 was captured.

Valkey's internal state could not be read: redis_info against the configured Redis/Valkey target returned REDIS_AUTH_FAILED, so requirepass/ACL settings, connected_clients, memory and errorstats for valkey-cart are unknown; whether valkey rejects unauthenticated new connections could not be verified.

No redis_* metric series exist in Prometheus (queries matching {__name__=~".*redis.*"} and {__name__=~"redis_.*|valkey.*"} returned nothing; the app-namespace collector's metrics pipeline exports only to debug), so valkey health cannot be measured from metrics.

Queries for traces_span_metrics_calls_total with namespace="astronomy-shop" or k8s_namespace_name="astronomy-shop" returned no data; only the series listing without a namespace filter and a per-service sum for cart (one sample at 10:22:13) were available, so service error-rate ratios could not be computed.

No error-rate or latency baseline exists for this environment: all 23 Deployments were created 2026-11-24T10:21:09Z and traces_span_metrics_* series first appear at 10:22:13, so no before/after trend is claimed.

Several views this Run relied on were themselves incomplete (the cart trace search, the frontend error trace search, the collector logs and the all-series listing hit result or line limits), so spans and log lines outside those sampled slices remain unknown.

Whether other pods on node sregym-worker can currently open new connections to valkey-cart on sregym-worker2 could not be tested (no exec or probe tool), so the blast radius of the connection-path fault is unknown.

The exact trigger of the previous cart pod's deletion at 10:21:52 (pod-level kill versus eviction versus controller action) is unknown; no Evicted event and no owning-controller SuccessfulDelete/SuccessfulCreate pair were observed for that pod.
